title: Miten and kuinka: answering about manner
summary: Miten asks how something happens. Miten sinä puhut? — Puhun hitaasti.
targetSkills: Miten and kuinka: answering about manner
objectives: Ask how an action happens with miten or kuinka.
Describe the action with the appropriate manner word.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants.
Miten asks how something happens. Kuinka can ask about manner too in these examples, although the two words are not interchangeable in every Finnish expression.
keyPoints: Do not use miksi when the requested information is how, rather than why.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Answer with a manner word, often an adverb, which tells how an action happens: hyvin (“well”), hitaasti (“slowly”), nopeasti (“quickly”) or selvästi (“clearly”). The adjective describing a person and the adverb describing an action are different: hidas (“slow”) becomes hitaasti (“slowly”), with the weak d changing to t in this stem.
A natural short reply to “Miten sinä puhut?” is “Hitaasti.” (“Slowly.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
To correct a suggested manner, reject it with the complete negative phrase en puhu and give the actual manner. Keep the manner adverb rather than replacing it with an adjective.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Describe the action with the manner form, not a yes/no reply or an unrelated place.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: hitaasti means slowly here. Hidas uses the strong long-vowel stem hitaa- with -sti: hitaasti; d changes to t.
selvästi means clearly here. Selvä + -sti gives selvästi.
nopeasti means quickly here. Nopea + -sti gives nopeasti, describing the action rather than a person.

steps: Miten: how; question asking how the action happens. Miten asks about manner or method in these examples.
sinä: you; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Sinä addresses one person informally.
puhut: you speak; verb (the action or state). Puhu- + singular second-person -t gives puhut.
Puhun: I speak; verb (the action or state). Puhua removes final -a and adds -n: puhu- + -n gives puhun.

examples.english: I do not speak slowly. I speak clearly.
steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
puhu: speak; main verb after the negative verb. Remove -n from puhun to obtain negative puhu, with no personal ending.
hitaasti: slowly; manner. Hidas uses the strong long-vowel stem hitaa- with -sti: hitaasti; d changes to t.
Puhun: I speak; verb (the action or state). Puhua removes final -a and adds -n: puhu- + -n gives puhun.
selvästi: clearly; manner. Selvä + -sti gives selvästi.
